newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police hunt for stolen Cartier bracelet.
newsitem.headline: Italian police hunt for stolen Cartier bracelet.

text.p: Italian police were hunting on Friday for a sapphire and diamond Cartier bracelet valued at $2 million after it was stolen from a jewellery collection on show at one of Milan's most exclusive hotels.
The platinum bracelet, made by world famous French jewellery house Cartier in 1923, was one of 550 pieces on view at the Four Seasons Hotel in the exclusive Montenapoleone shopping district.
Security guards at the exhibition raised the alarm on Thursday afternoon after discovering the lock of a display case had been forced open and the bracelet removed.
Guards immediately shut the doors to the show rooms preventing 70 visitors to the exhibition from leaving before the police arrived.
"We are continuing to question the people who were present but so far we're stumped," a police spokesman said.

The stolen bracelet, described as belonging to the Art Deco period, is owned by a U.S. family and had been part of the exhibition of pieces from private collections all over the world which had been displayed in Paris, London, New York, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Dubai and Beirut.

The piece was due to be auctioned by Antiquorum Auctioneers on November 19 in Geneva with other Cartier works including pieces once belonging to Egypt's King Farouk, Morocco's King Hassan, the late pop artist Andy Warhol and Woolworth heiress Barbara Hutton.
